reason: Endeavour's origin from spare parts, record-setting space missions, and epic 12-mile urban LA street haul provide ample multi-sourced claims for a mind-bending short.
story: After the 1986 Challenger tragedy, NASA constructed Space Shuttle Endeavour using spare structural parts built for Discovery and Atlantis. Named by school students after Captain James Cook's exploration ship, Endeavour flew 25 space missions, executing the first Hubble Space Telescope repair and an unprecedented three-person spacewalk to retrieve a stranded satellite. Over its career, the orbiter logged nearly 123 million miles and spent 299 days in space. Following its final flight in 2011, NASA retired Endeavour to the California Science Center in Los Angeles. In October 2012, after arriving atop a modified Boeing 747, the 170,000-pound spacecraft undertook a painstaking 12-mile journey through city streets. Creeping at top speeds of 2 mph over 68 hours, crews cut down over 400 trees, temporarily removed traffic signals, and turned off power lines as Endeavour squeezed past buildings with mere inches of clearance.
angle: To reach its museum home, a 170,000-pound space shuttle was navigated 12 miles through urban Los Angeles streets, requiring over 400 trees to be cut down and squeezing past apartment buildings with inches of clearance.

claims.claim: Congress authorized building Endeavour in 1987 to replace the destroyed Space Shuttle Challenger.
Endeavour was assembled using structural spare parts manufactured during the construction of Discovery and Atlantis.
NASA selected the name Endeavour through a national competition among elementary and secondary schools.
President George H. W. Bush selected and announced the winning name Endeavour.
Endeavour was named after HMS Endeavour, the 18th-century British ship captained by James Cook.
Endeavour launched on its first space mission, STS-49, in May 1992.
During mission STS-49, astronauts performed a historic three-person spacewalk to capture the Intelsat VI satellite.
Endeavour flew the first servicing mission to repair the Hubble Space Telescope during STS-61 in 1993.
Endeavour was constructed with a 40-foot drag chute to reduce its landing rollout distance.
Endeavour completed 25 space missions before decommissioning after its final flight in 2011.
Over its flight career, Endeavour traveled nearly 123 million miles in space.
NASA awarded Endeavour to the California Science Center in Los Angeles for permanent display.
Endeavour arrived at LAX mounted on top of a modified Boeing 747 Shuttle Carrier Aircraft in September 2012.
In October 2012, Endeavour embarked on a 12-mile overland transport through the streets of Los Angeles.
Crews removed over 400 street trees in Los Angeles to clear a path for the shuttle's wide wingspan.
Workers temporarily turned off electric power lines and removed traffic signals along the transport route.
Endeavour's wingtips squeezed past city obstacles like apartment buildings and utility poles with inches of clearance.
The street haul through Los Angeles took 68 hours, moving at maximum speeds of roughly 2 mph.
The California Science Center built a display exhibiting Endeavour vertically in a full launch stack.
The vertical exhibit stack includes ET-94, the last flight-qualified external tank in existence.
Northrop Grumman donated flight-proven solid rocket booster components used on past shuttle flights for the exhibit.

disputed: Total days in space: S1, S5, and S7 state Endeavour spent 299 days in space, whereas S3 states 296 days, 3 hours. Script should state 'nearly 300 days in space' to remain accurate across sources.

External tank sea rescue detail: S1 mentions ET-94 rescued 4 people from a sinking fishing boat during its ocean barge transport to LA, which S4, S5, and S6 omit. Attribute as 'according to NASA records' if included, or leave out.
